authoritative_for: Weaver owns authored Markdown, exact authoring requests, one pending mailbox reply per document, observed execution outcomes, reading configuration, and deployment admission.
not_authoritative_for: Annals owns accepted source documents. Krisis owns decision identification. Nucleus owns execution, authentication, and its retained history. The agent owns editorial interpretation under the user direction.

covers: All Weaver authoring, revision, resume, document reads, configuration, readiness, maintained installation, and development outcomes.
excludes: Help/version, factual certification, citations, source inventories, source mutation, publication, email, scheduling, automatic retries, and retired Weaver workflows.

shared_access_and_trust: Private current-user local CLI and SQLite. The author can only read accepted Annals documents and submit Markdown; workspace, shell, and web are disabled.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Requests, documents, and pending tool replies are private. Nucleus may retain full source reads. Weaver clears acknowledged replies and keeps documents and invocation records without automatic pruning.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. Chancery records command identity, time, and thread ID in its private journal. Arguments, output, outcomes, and internal product calls are excluded. Recording errors do not change command results.
compatibility_and_retirement: Independent release, SQLite schema 1, and weaver/narrative toolsets: historical version 1 and new selection version plus 1. No legacy workflow or database import is provided. Historical execution registrations retain their meaning.
operational_limits: One foreground runner handles up to the requested positive number of concurrent job loops in write-many. Each document has one job, a 1200-second active attempt limit, and a 1800-second observation deadline from its Nucleus attempt start. Queue time consumes neither limit; resume preserves the job deadline. Dependency command latency remains unbounded. Annals pages contain at most 200 documents and 4 MiB of text. Markdown is at most 1 MiB. No latency or research-completeness guarantee.
